newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas rises on cold weather forecast.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas rises on cold weather forecast.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices strengthened Friday on prospects of colder temperatures in eastern Canada, market sources said.
At Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, swing prices were up nearly 20 cents to the $3.95-4.00 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range.
A cold front is expected to cover the eastern third of North America next week.
Also triggering a price increase was the rally in the NYMEX market, where January natgas futures jumped to a new contract high of $3.87, up 34.1 cents from the previous settlement.
At Sumas, Wash., the Canada-U.S. border, spot prices gained about 20 cents to the $3.15-3.20 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) area.
Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest are forecast to dip to about four to eight degrees Fahrenheit below-normal on Monday.
Spot prices at the AECO storage hub rose by about three cents to the high-C$1.80s per gigajoule (GJ).
January prices at AECO were talked in the C$2.09-2.11 per GJ range, up only marginally from December's index.
